questions.prompt: G2 BRIEF — atlas-net (ASP.NET Core EOR platform, 438 xUnit tests). Practice exercise 4 asks you to prove the payroll snapshot: run payroll for a month, raise the worker's salary, re-read the run — the payslips must still show the old salary. You want a coding agent to turn that into a permanent regression test for a COMPLETED run. This is a tests-only delegation. Write the brief: goal, allowed files, boundaries, test command, stop condition. Commit to your brief first, then tick the checkpoints you covered and add up the weights.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal: an integration test that completes a run, then approves a raise effective inside that month, then re-reads the run and its invoice and asserts the old salary and the original invoice total.
keyPoints.quote: Run payroll for a month, then raise the worker's salary, then re-read the completed run's payslips.

keyPoints.text: [w3] The brief points at existing coverage first: the DRAFT-run variant already exists, so the new test must target the completed-run path and not duplicate it.
[w2] Allowed files: PayrollEdgeCaseTests.cs only, reusing its private helpers (country, hire, run, amendment) rather than new fixtures.
[w3] Boundary: no production code changes. If the new test FAILS, that is a snapshot-contract violation to report with the failing assertion, not something to 'fix' in PayrollService.
[w2] Boundary: use a country/currency no other test uses; FX rates and countries are shared inside the class fixture's database, so reused codes leak state across tests.
[w2] Test command: the single-class filter while iterating, then the full `dotnet test`.
[w2] Stop condition: new test green, suite count 438 + 1, nothing else changed; stop at the first unexpected failure and hand back the output.

questions.prompt: G2 PRE-MORTEM — same delegation. How might the agent go wrong on this tests-only task, and which line of your brief prevents it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] It approves the raise BEFORE creating the run, so the test proves salary history selection instead of the snapshot.
[w2] It asserts only on GrossSalary and forgets the invoice, missing the audit consequence the exercise is about.
keyPoints.quote: says why an invoice that recomputed from live data would be an audit incident.

keyPoints.text: [w2] It sees a red test and 'helpfully' adds a recalculation path, a feature the ADR explicitly rules out.
[w2] It hard-codes expected totals without the employer-cost and fee arithmetic the sibling test spells out, so the number is unexplained.
[w1] It writes a new WebApplicationFactory instead of the class fixture, slowing the suite and diverging from the isolated in-memory SQLite setup.

questions.prompt: G2 HANDBACK REVIEW — the agent says the test is in and green. What do you verify before accepting?

keyPoints.text: [w3] Mutation check: temporarily make the run's GET recompute payslips from live salary instead of returning the stored ones, and confirm the new test goes red; a test that cannot fail proves nothing.
[w2] The diff is one test method in PayrollEdgeCaseTests.cs; no src/ file appears.
[w2] The order of operations in the test is create run, complete run, then approve the raise, then re-read.
[w2] The run output shows the full-suite total rising by exactly one.
[w1] The handback states the real-world rule the test pins (payslips and invoices are stable historical records) in one sentence.
